html:
Genghis Khan, born Temüjin around 1162, was the founder and first khan of the Mongol Empire. He united the tribes of the Mongolian steppe and led conquests in China and Central Asia that began the largest land empire in history.

His youth was hard. His father, a minor chief, died when Temüjin was a boy, and his family was abandoned by their tribe. He won followers and allies, rescued his wife Börte from raiders, and slowly rose. He fought his former friend Jamukha and his patron Toghrul, and by 1205 had beaten every rival on the steppe.

In 1206 an assembly proclaimed him Genghis Khan. He then rebuilt Mongol society:

  • He broke up the old tribes and organised the army in units of tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands, led by men chosen for loyalty.
  • He issued laws later known as the Yassa.
  • He adopted the Uyghur script for writing Mongolian.

His campaigns:

  • 1205 to 1209: raids and war against Western Xia in northwest China, which submitted.
  • 1211 onward: against the Jin dynasty in north China; Zhongdu, today's Beijing, fell in 1215.
  • 1219 to 1221: the invasion of Khwarazm, which destroyed the great cities of Central Asia.

He died in 1227 during a last campaign against Western Xia. His grave is unknown. His son Ögedei succeeded him. The Secret History of the Mongols tells his life from the Mongol side.
sum: Genghis Khan, born Temüjin around 1162, was the founder and first khan of the Mongol Empire. He united the tribes of the Mongolian steppe and led conquests in China and Central Asia that began the largest land empire in history.
